content: 1. Universal health coverage and community engagement were discussed in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2018, volume 96, issue 9, pages 660–661. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a practical tool in 2016 to strengthen gender-sensitive national HIV and Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) monitoring and evaluation systems. 3. The Clinical and Translational Science Awards Consortium Community Engagement Key Function Committee Task Force outlined principles of community engagement in a document published by the NIH in 2011 (Publication No. 11-7782). 4. The 69th World Health Assembly in May 2016 developed a framework for engagement with non-state actors, spanning pages 1–35. 5. Use and Hawkes explored the role of health within the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the potential for a paradigm shift in a 2015 article in Global Health, volume 11, issue 1, pages 1–8. 6. The United Nations outlined the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in 2015, with specific focus on health, available online. 7. Carter, Tregear, and Lachance conducted a systematic review published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in August 2015, volume 49, supplement 2, pages S116–S123. 8. O’Mara-Eves and colleagues performed a meta-analysis in 2015 on the effectiveness of community engagement in public health interventions for disadvantaged groups, published in BMC Public Health, volume 15, article 129. 9. The WHO, in collaboration with the United Nations Population Fund, UNAIDS, the Global Network of Sex Work Projects, and the World Bank, published a guide in 2013 on implementing comprehensive HIV/STI programs with sex workers. 10. The ALIV[H]E framework, developed by the Salamander Trust, UNAIDS, and others in 2019, provided key examples of initiatives addressing violence against women and HIV. 11. 12. The WHO published its Evaluation Practice Handbook in 2013 to guide evaluation processes. 13. The WHO released the second edition of its Handbook for Guideline Development in 2014, providing comprehensive guidance for creating health-related guidelines. 14. In 2017, the WHO published a consolidated guideline on the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women living with HIV, spanning 144 pages. 15. Orza, Welbourn, Bewley, Crone, and Vazquez presented findings from a global survey on values and preferences in 2014, emphasizing the importance of building a safe foundation for health initiatives. 16. The WHO published an overview of integrated care models in 2016 as part of its Health Services Delivery Program, available online. 17. The WHO Secretariat released a framework on integrated, people-centered health services in 2016, emphasizing the importance of holistic care approaches. 18. The WHO developed a toolkit in 2017 to support individuals, families, and communities in improving maternal and newborn health. 19. Dye, Boerma, Evans, Harries, Lienhardt, McManus, Pang, Terry, and Zachariah contributed to the 2013 World Health Report, which focused on research for achieving universal health coverage. 20. Kelly, Morgan, Bonnefoy, Butt, Bergman, Mackenbach, and colleagues created a guide in 2007 to construct an evidence base on the social determinants of health, published by the WHO. 21. Frohlich and Potvin discussed the inequality paradox in public health practice, emphasizing the population approach and vulnerable populations, in a 2008 article in the American Journal of Public Health, volume 98, issue 2, pages 216–221.
